transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-19
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Derek Silva (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO, Granite), Priya Patel (Head Eng), Marco Ruiz (Data Eng)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Discussed pricing and cost levers; agreed to run benchmark; Redwood to send pricing and TCO sheet; customer to share prompt mix and volumes.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Derek, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:08] Liam: Hey Maya, good thanks. Priya and Marco here as well. Short on time for everyone, appreciate it.
[00:13] Priya: Hi all. We're doing cost discovery mostly — trying to under- stand what Hosted vs Dedicated looks like for our workloads.
[00:21] Derek: Great — we'll focus on per-token economics, batching, caching, and some ways to bring down unit cost while keeping latency SLOs.
[00:28] Marco: Quick intro — we run a customer support summarization pipeline and a real-time agent assist system. Spike loads during business hours, about 60M tokens/month right now, hoping to get to 200M in 3 quarters. Budget target: roughly $10k - $15k/month for inference.
[00:45] Maya: Got it. That's helpful. Can you confirm mix — how much is short chat vs long summarization?
[00:51] Marco: Roughly 70% short-turn chat (<128 tokens), 30% long summarization (avg 800-1,000 tokens).
[00:58] Derek: Ok that mix matters a lot for batching and KV cache efficiency. For hosted we publish per-token rates — for smaller models/econ models pricing may be as low as $0.0002 per token output for embeddings-style, but for large 8k-16k generation models it's higher. For dedicated, unit cost effectively drops because you amortize GPU; depends on utilization.
[01:22] Liam: Can you give a ballpark? Our rough calc right now says $0.0008/output-token on our current setup — that's painful at scale. We want to see if Redwood can be half that.
[01:33] Derek: Ballpark scenarios: on Hosted, for a Llama2-like 7B quantized runtime with good batching and caching, you might see $0.0004-$0.0006 per output token end-to-end including network and infra surcharge. Dedicated reserved capacity with sustained 60-80% utilization could push cost closer to $0.00015-$0.00035 per token, but there are commit/seat fees.
[01:56] Priya: That delta is big, but we can't always hit high utilization because of spiky traffic. Any levers to reduce cost without dedicated?
[02:05] Derek: Yes — three primary levers: batching configuration, prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts, and model quantization/selection. Batching groups concurrent requests to amortize forward-pass cost; you can tune max latency vs batch window. Prefix caching stores KV cache for common prefixes — huge win for chat where the beginning of conversation repeats. Quantization (4-bit/8-bit) can reduce GPU memory and allow cheaper instance types.
[02:36] Marco: For our agent assist, lots of repeated system prompt + few-shot examples. We could benefit from prefix caching. How much savings realistically?
[02:43] Derek: For repeated prefixes that are 30-40% of token compute, caching can cut token compute for those requests by 20-50% depending on hit rate. If 70% of your requests hit cache, net per-token compute cost goes down a lot.
[02:58] Maya: Also routing policies — you can route low-risk traffic to cheaper model variants (quantized 7B) and high-risk to 13B or hosted premium. That's a common hybrid.
[03:09] Liam: We're also worried about latency SLOs — agent assist needs sub-300ms tail. Does caching/batching help or hurt latency?
[03:18] Derek: Batching introduces a small queueing delay; you can configure max batch latency 20-100ms. For sub-300ms tail, you can use a small batch window + preemptive routing to lower-latency nodes, or dedicate capacity sized for tail SLO. Also enable streaming so tokens start returning earlier.
[03:35] Priya: On Dedicated, what's the minimum commit size? If we need to guarantee latency, we might consider dedicated but concerned about up-front cost.
[03:44] Maya: Typical small dedicated pool starts at a few GPUs equivalent; exact commit depends on region and instance type. We model the commitment vs pay-as-you-go math in the TCO sheet — we'll include sample scenarios for your 60M -> 200M growth curve.
[03:58] Marco: Can the platform autoscale for spikes if we have dedicated + burst?
[04:03] Derek: Yes — Dedicated supports burst to hosted capacity and autoscale policies, but bursting has different cost characteristics. We'll detail that in the pricing sheet.
[04:12] Liam: Security is also important — we need SOC2, SAML SSO, customer-managed KMS and audit logs.
[04:19] Maya: We're SOC 2 Type II, support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS integrations. We'll attach our security docs.
[04:25] Priya: Good. Back to cost, what about quantization tradeoffs on output quality? We can't degrade NPS-critical responses.
[04:33] Derek: Right — quantization can introduce small quality regressions, especially on instruction-following or generation diversity. We recommend running evals on your prompt sets: Redwood Optimize will propose quantization profiles and model variants with regression thresholds. For pilot, we can run head-to-head comparisons: 7B-quantized vs 13B-fp16 on your top 50 prompts.
[04:55] Marco: Sounds useful. How long does a benchmark take?
[04:59] Derek: For 50 prompts across three temperature/params, a full run could be done in 24-48 hours depending on quota. We'll need your prompt set and expected concurrency to size.
[05:08] Liam: Ok — our rough budget of $10k/month — any simple model mix that hits that for 60M tokens?
[05:16] Derek: Quick back-of-envelope: if you average $0.00025 per output token (dedicated-like efficiency), 60M tokens is $15k. To reach $10k you'd need $0.000166 per token. Achievable by combining cheaper model routing + caching + batching. Example: route 50% to cheap quantized 7B at $0.00008/token equivalent, 30% to 13B quantized at $0.00025, 20% to high-quality hosted at $0.0006 — blended could be around $0.00025. To get lower, you'd need higher cache hit rates or higher utilization on dedicated.
[05:54] Priya: So immediate wins are: move repetitive parts to cache, route low-risk flows to quantized models, and then assess dedicated when volume grows.
[06:03] Maya: Exactly. We'll include scenario tables in the sheet.
[06:07] Marco: Any notes on network egress or hidden costs?
[06:11] Derek: For hosted there are platform surcharges that we include; dedicated may have infra egress costs depending on private VPC setup. We'll call out explicit line items.
[06:21] Liam: One more: can we run vantage benchmarks with our data in a private VPC so PII doesn't leave environment?
[06:29] Derek: Yes — for sensitive data we can deploy a private pilot in your VPC or on-prem option; that affects setup time and may shift to Private deployment contract. We'll outline that option.
[06:39] Priya: Timeline — we want a pilot within 2-3 weeks if possible. Is that realistic?
[06:44] Maya: If you share prompt set and sample traffic this week, we can stand up a benchmark next week and run it for a few days. Then demo results and recommended config.
[06:55] Marco: We'll try to get that over by Friday.
[06:58] Derek: Great. Recap of technical asks: sample prompts, concurrency, token volumes, and top error cases. We'll return a benchmark plan.
[07:08] Liam: On the pricing side, can you show both hosted per-token and a dedicated reservation amortized over different utilization scenarios (50/70/90%)?
[07:16] Maya: Absolutely — the TCO sheet will have amortized dedicated math and hosted per-token rows for model variants and quantization tiers.
[07:23] Priya: Also include an example of cost sensitivity to cache hit rate (e.g., 0%, 30%, 60%, 80%).
[07:31] Derek: Will do — and we'll show how caching affects effective throughput and request units.
[07:37] Marco: Any immediate blockers on our side? I think just sharing prompts and confirming pilot scope.
[07:42] Liam: Agree. Also who from Redwood will be our primary SE contact during pilot?
[07:46] Maya: Derek will be SE lead. I'm AE and will handle procurement/pricing/docs.
[07:51] Priya: Noted. A couple of quick clarifying Qs: do you charge for inactive model versions in Dedicated?
[07:57] Derek: You pay for reserved capacity, but model versions don't incur extra unless you exceed capacity or use additional GPU types. We'll note that nuance.
[08:06] Maya: Also worth noting we have intelligent routing that can fail over to a fallback model during capacity constraints, which can help keep the app online.
[08:15] Liam: Good. Any compliance checklist for Private (VPC/on-prem) pilot?
[08:20] Derek: We'll attach our Private deployment checklist — networking, KMS keys, audit log endpoints, and account provisioning. Setup typically takes 2-4 weeks depending on approvals.
[08:31] Priya: Hmm might be tight for the 2-3 week pilot but okay if we do hosted benchmark first.
[08:37] Maya: Makes sense. We'll propose hosted benchmark first, then if results warrant a private pilot, we move to that.
[08:44] Marco: Pricing sensitivity — do you offer ramped discounts or volume tiers as we commit to more tokens?
[08:50] Maya: Yes — reserved/dedicated pricing is tiered; we can model a stepped discount curve in the sheet and show break-even points.
[08:58] Liam: Great. Anything else on the cost levers we missed?
[09:01] Derek: One more: response truncation and token limits. For long summarization you can pre-trim context or run a two-stage pipeline (extractive then generative) to reduce output tokens. That often yields big savings.
[09:15] Priya: We're doing some extractive prefiltering today; might push more to that.
[09:18] Marco: Ok that helps.
[09:20] Maya: Quick logistics: we'll send pricing/TCO, security docs, and Derek's benchmark plan. You'll send prompts and volumes. Follow-up call week of 2026-03-30. Any conflicts?
[09:32] Liam: Works for us.
[09:33] Priya: Works.
[09:35] Marco: Fine here.
[09:36] Maya: Awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with artifacts.
[09:42] Liam: Thanks all.
